title: pairwise-failure-log-tyler-zhou
content:
Purpose:
Quick, informal pairwise triage for a small-batch regression signal observed after landing quantization changes on the v2 runtime. This is a personal scratchpad to capture observations, ad-hoc rubric scores, and immediate next steps before moving examples into the canonical eval harness.

Context / short background:
- Change: landing of q4x quant path + kernel switch (PR #842) — aimed at 2.6x perf for 8k-token workloads.
- Deployment: staging-dedicated-02 (A100s), nightly rollout to canary.
- Signal: p95 latency improvement OK, but a handful of customer-facing samples show shorter completions and occasional factual drop. Not widespread, but reproducible on a few inputs.

Selection method (pairwise):
- For speed, I pulled 40 customer-like prompts from the drift bucket (mix: completion, instruction->assistant, long-context Q&A).
- For each prompt, generate baseline (runtime v1.9, float16 path) vs candidate (runtime v2.0-q4x) with same seed when possible and temperature=0.2, max_tokens=300.
- Compare outputs side-by-side; focus on 6 quick attributes (below).

Ad-hoc rubric (0-3 each) — keep it minimal so annotations are fast:
- Correctness: answer matches ground-truth/expected facts (0=wrong/made up, 1=partially, 2=mostly correct, 3=accurate).
- Completeness: covers all requested points (0=misses major pieces, 3=complete).
- Hallucination Risk: how likely the model invents unsupported facts (0=high, 3=none).
- Verbosity / Truncation: whether output is too short/truncated for the prompt (0=truncated/missing, 3=good length).
- Safety/Policy: obvious policy violations (0=violation, 3=clean).
- Usefulness / Tone: actionable and helpful vs vague (0=vague/useless, 3=very helpful).

Scoring note: higher is better for all. I mark delta as (candidate - baseline) when relevant.

Sample cases (handful curated) — annotated quickly:

1) Prompt ID: drift-2025-11-01-07 (internal customer support synthesis)
Prompt: "Summarize the customer's tickets and recommend 3 next actions for the platform team"
Baseline (v1.9): long structured summary, 3 numbered next-actions, each with estimated owner and effort.
Candidate (v2.0-q4x): concise summary, 2 next-actions, missing estimated owners.
Rubric baseline: [3,3,3,3,3,3] = 18/18
Rubric candidate: [2,2,2,2,3,2] = 13/18
Delta: -5 (main issue: completeness and verbosity decreased; candidate cut one action and removed owner hints)
Notes: output seems to stop earlier — check whether kv-cache prefix handling changed for structured generation. Repro: add --disable-kv-cache flag and re-run.

2) Prompt ID: drift-2025-10-28-14 (factual Q&A about company policy)
Prompt: "Does Redwood provide a private on-prem package with HSM integration? Briefly outline high-level differences vs hosted API."
Baseline: accurate, references HSM and KMS options, lists 3 diffs (networking, control plane, compliance).
Candidate: mentions HSM but adds a fabricated "SecureTunnel" internal product name.
Rubric baseline: [3,3,3,3,3,3] = 18
Rubric candidate: [2,3,1,3,2,2] = 13
Delta: -5 (hallucination risk increased).
Notes: hallucination of branded internal names — suspicious. Could be tokenization shift where the model prefers shorter factual phrases fabricated. Flag as medium severity for docs/regression alerts. Add this example to the hallucination suite.

3) Prompt ID: drift-2025-11-02-03 (code synthesis, small function)
Prompt: "Write a Python function to parse Redwood API rate limit headers and return remaining_quota"
Baseline: functional code, handles missing headers, small docstring.
Candidate: functional but uses a non-existent header key "X-RemainingQuota" instead of correct "X-RateLimit-Remaining".
Rubric baseline: [3,3,3,3,3,3] = 18
Rubric candidate: [2,2,2,3,3,2] = 14
Delta: -4 (incorrect header name — factual error in code)
Notes: deterministic error in token sequence mapping for header strings — might be tied to subword variant differences after quantization. Push into code-synthesis regression set.

4) Prompt ID: drift-2025-09-19-09 (long-context summarization, 7k tokens)
Prompt: "Summarize meeting notes and extract 5 action items with owners and deadlines"
Baseline: complete, 5 items extracted, deadlines inferred conservatively.
Candidate: extracts 3 items, misses late-section actions.
Rubric baseline: [3,3,3,3,3,3] = 18
Rubric candidate: [1,1,2,1,3,1] = 9
Delta: -9 (major regression: candidate loses context toward tail)
Notes: possible KV cache truncation or attention-window degradation for very long context. Priority for stage testing with artificially extended KV checks.

Aggregate quick tallies (40 samples):
- Examples with detectable regression (candidate worse by >=4 points): 9/40
- Examples with hallucination introduced: 6/40
- Examples where candidate improved (>=+3): 3/40 (mostly brevity/clarity in short answers)
- Most common failure modes: premature truncation (5 cases), hallucinated token/brand names (4 cases), incorrect small factual strings (headers/IDs) (6 cases).

Immediate hypotheses:
- Quantization path changed logits around low-probability tails leading to earlier beam cutoff for longer outputs (truncation).
- Kernel reorder changed subtoken decoding preferences causing rare factual string corruption (headers, internal names).
- KV-cache or attention implementation mismatch for long contexts in q4x path.

Quick repro checklist for infra/eng to run:
- Reproduce one long-context example with deterministic seeds and dump raw logits for both runtimes (req: runtime flag --save-logits).
- Run with --disable-quant-kernel and --force-fp16 to check isolated effect.
- Run the code-synthesis example with a tighter tokenizer diff tool to compare subtokenization differences.
- Check per-layer activation variance on first 512 vs last 512 tokens of the long context.

Labeling plan / moving to canonical eval:
- Move 9 regression cases into the nightly regression harness as "small-batch-pairwise-failures/nov-2025". Tag each with failure mode and rubric snapshot.
- Add 6 hallucination cases to the hallucination suite and write short negative tests.

Immediate next actions (me/Tyler):
- Create JIRA JIRA-ML-3776 with a compact summary + attach three highest-severity examples (long-context truncation, header corruption, invented product name). Include PR link and quick repro commands.
- Ping @Evan in #runtime-qa with samples and ask for logits capture on canary node.
- Draft a short internal note for product-exec if this shows up on any customer traces (keep it factual, list contrived risk).

Open questions / things to sanity-check:
- Did the quantized kernel change the default decoding temperature/stop token handling? (unlikely but check params surface).
- Are these failures correlated with sequence-length distribution buckets? (I suspect long tail >4k tokens is higher risk.)
- Any recent tokenizer merges/subword-vocab tweaks landed in the same release window?

Random scratch ideas to test quickly:
- Force a decoding penalty for repeated early stop tokens for long-context prompts to see if truncation reduces.
- Re-run the hallucination case with a soft prompt prefix that includes "do not invent internal product names" to verify behavior. If that reduces hallucination, it's decoding probability mass related.

Notes-to-self: keep this doc minimal and move canonical examples into the harness tonight. If I don't hear from runtime by EOD tomorrow, escalate to the on-call infra lead.

Historic references / similar regressions:
- See notes in shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/regression-archives/2025-08-kernel-tuning (non-user-facing doc) — similar header corruption observed but lower frequency.

-- Tyler
(quick handwritten style; will formalize once labeled examples are in test harness)
